items.title: Besieged Yemeni city on verge of ‘unmanageable’ crisis, aid workers warn
items.summary: Water and fresh food running out in Taiz as fighting intensifies and Houthi advance cuts off most supply routes The humanitarian crisis in the besieged Yemeni city of Taiz is becoming unmanageable as the city runs out of water, fuel and fresh food, Oxfam aid workers in the country have warned. Iran-allied Houthi forces have largely encircled the city of more than 900,000 people, cutting it off from most supply routes. This week, heavy fighting has raged around the city’s old airport, causing extensive damage in a densely populated residential area. Continue reading...

items.title: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz
items.summary: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz The United Nations insisted on Tuesday that aid must immediately be allowed to enter Yemen's Taiz, besieged by Iran-aligned Houthi fighters who are preventing supplies from reaching the country's third-largest city. Houthi fighters have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, interim capital of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government. "Humanitarian aid must be immediately allowed to enter the city and its passage must be facilitated," UN human rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement. He said relief must reach the city to avert a rights catastrophe. "The Houthis' closure of the only supply route linking Taiz to Aden is placing civilians at grave risk, blocking humanitarian aid and cutting off essential supplies," said Turk.

items.summary: IRGC says three tankers hit mines crossing Hormuz Strait Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Tuesday that its naval mines halted three tankers attempting to travel the Strait of Hormuz via routes considered illegal by Tehran. "Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the IRGC said in a statement on its official Sepah News website. The Guard later said in a statement carried by state TV that a third oil tanker "exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz". The statement added that the tanker, "carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil, had deactivated all of its radar and navigation systems".

items.title: UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia
items.summary: UN Security Council condemns 'escalatory' Houthi strikes on Saudi Arabia The UN Security Council has condemned the "escalatory" attacks by Iran-backed Houthis on Saudi Arabia, including "reckless strikes" on Riyadh's airport. The Saudi capital's international airport has been targeted by strikes 20 times since the beginning of the month, with an attack last weekend killing 13 people and wounding more than 300. In a joint statement shared by the Security Council's president, Greece's Evangelos Sekeris, the 15-member UN body also condemned "continued Houthi attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab (Strait)". The statement also "affirmed the inherent right of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of self-defence in accordance with international law."

items.summary: Iran's IRGC navy says oil tanker hits mine, catches fire in Strait of Hormuz An oil tanker caught fire and exploded after striking a naval mine in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) navy said on Sunday, according to Iranian media. The vessel violated Iran-imposed “regulations” by switching off its navigation system while transiting the waterway, the IRGC said. “An illicit oil tanker exploded and caught fire in its engine room after hitting a naval mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz,” the Fars news agency quoted the IRGC as saying. “If ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf switch off their navigation and identification systems, they will be dealt with severely and decisively.”

clusters.headline: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen government camp rises to 73

items.title: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen government camp rises to 73
items.summary: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen government camp rises to 73 Local Yemeni authorities on Tuesday raised the death toll from a Houthi strike a day earlier on a military camp belonging to government forces to 73, as fighting between the foes escalates. It marked the deadliest attack in weeks as fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised, Saudi-supported government rages after the collapse of a years-long truce. The death toll from Monday's strike on the camp in the energy-rich Shabwa province "increased to 73 martyrs, while search and follow-up efforts are ongoing to discover the fate of 14 missing people", authorities said in a statement. Local authorities had put the death toll at 53 on Monday, adding that more than 200 others were injured, all new members of the internal security forces who were undergoing training.

The poll surveyed 156 people currently serving in the military, 431 veterans, and  144 immediate family members of active-duty service members between September 15 and 28. Common Defense is a veteran-led group that advocates for progressive policies and endorses Democratic candidates, though a 47% of respondents to their September poll are self-identified Republicans. Nearly 20% identified as “pure independents,” while 35% said they were Democrats. Though Republicans surveyed in the poll backed Operation Epic Fury at a rate of 77% to 16%, overwhelming opposition among Democrats and independents left respondents opposed to the war overall, 49% to 44%. items.title: How the UAE and MEK weaponize AI to spread propaganda
items.summary: Somewhere inside Iran, a network of activists exchanged messages about politics and news with an activist — nicknamed “Parsa” — on the messaging app Telegram. They had no idea they were actually speaking to an AI agent that had copied the real activist’s style by training it on 8,400 real Telegram posts. Instead of “Parsa,” they were actually communicating with the People’s Mojahedin Organization of Iran (MEK), an Iranian Islamist-Marxist opposition group widely regarded as a cult. According to a report from Anthropic released last month, this operation was carried out by four individuals working for the MEK. They built an AI agent named “Viktor” that also surveilled individuals inside Iran and flooded social media platforms with pro-MEK content under “independent” branding. The Anthropic report sheds light on how foreign actors are increasingly using artificial intelligence tools like Claude and ChatGPT for their influence operations. items.title: As Houthis encircle Taiz, Yemen's Saudi-backed gov't faces disaster
items.summary: Taiz, Yemen’s third-largest city, endured a siege from 2015 to 2017. Today, it is encircled again. The World Food Program says it cannot reach more than 600,000 people in and around the city. The International Organization for Migration counts over 200,000 people displaced since the Houthi offensive on Yemen’s Red Sea coast launched in September. Why this city, and why now? The Houthis, formally known as the Ansar Allah movement, draw their strength from the Zaydi Shia highlands of the north. Critics say their governing ideology rests on the belief that the right to rule belongs to sayyids , descendants of the Prophet Mohammad, a lineage to which the Houthi family itself belongs. The Houthis have long denied seeking to restore the Imamate, but in Taiz, which has for a decade resisted Houthi encroachment, that denial finds few believers. Taiz has a long history of political activism and hostility to the idea of religious hereditary rule. items.title: The Fog of Tech

Vooral de vraag wat er na de Amerikaanse tussentijdse verkiezingen van 3 november gebeurt tussen Amerika en Iran houdt de Golfregio bezig. items.title: Iran’s attacks on Hormuz shipping 'unsuccessful', Centcom says
items.summary: Iran’s attacks on Hormuz shipping 'unsuccessful', Centcom says The US military says the “vast majority” of Iran’s attempted attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz have failed, and that the waterway remains open. On Saturday, US Central Command spokesperson Tim Hawkins told Fox News that about 97 percent of vessels trying to cross the strait had done so without being struck, many of them with US military protection. “What the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps of Iran is doing is unjustified and it’s also unsuccessful because they are not achieving their objective of closing the Strait of Hormuz,” Hawkins said.

items.title: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief
items.summary: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief The Strait of Hormuz "is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran ", the head of US Central Command (Centcom) has said. In a video statement, Centcom commander Brad Cooper said the US blockade of Iranian ports had imposed "a devastating cost" on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He said it had completely halted Iran's maritime exports and imports, "with the exception of humanitarian assistance we have allowed in". Cooper said the US had "prevented Iran from exporting at least 25 billion dollars worth of crude oil" and had "significantly degraded Iran's ability to project power far beyond its borders". He added that US forces had helped Gulf allies ship more than 100 million barrels of crude through the strait in the past week, with around 400 merchant vessels passing through. In total, the US had helped regional partners move 1.3 billion barrels through Hormuz in recent months, he said.

items.summary: US weighs lifting sanctions on Iran's 'shadow fleet' to address surging costs The US is considering lifting sanctions on “shadow fleet” tankers tied to Russia and Iran to address soaring diesel prices ahead of midterm elections, according to multiple reports and a senior US official. US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said in a video address to an energy forum in Riyadh this week that the Trump administration was discussing easing sanctions on shadow fleet vessels to address record freight rates that have driven up costs of shipping American energy abroad, Energy Aspects, a research group, said. The Financial Times reported on Thursday that the US could allow the sale of blacklisted vessels to non-sanctioned operators and lift sanctions, allowing them to operate without restrictions. Reuters reported the US could allow “legal oil" to flow on previously sanctioned vessels, effectively allowing sanctioned ships to carry crude or petroleum products not sanctioned by the US. items.title: La poesía no ha muerto
items.summary: Dice Andrés Trapiello que la poesía no ha muerto, esto es que vive, pero no así el mundo que la necesitaba. Lo dice, a su manera, para celebrar un aniversario de la editorial La Veleta, que el escritor fundó hace ahora cien libros de poemas, después de otras aventuras editoriales, como Trieste. Y lo celebra con la publicación de las traducciones de Emily Dickinson que debemos a Carlos Pujol, lector y traductor y persona inmejorable. Que el mundo haya necesitado la poesía alguna vez es una interesante hipótesis que muchos hechos podrían desmentir. O muchos versos: la flor que el arado destroza en el poema de Catulo, las cuatro personas para las que escribía Pound (¡oh mundo, lo siento por ti!), la tumba en el aire que excavan los judíos de la ‘Fuga de la muerte’ de Celan, o el combatiente ejecutado ante los ojos de René Char, caído como una hoja que una ráfaga de viento arrastraría... O la misma ausencia que Omar Jayyam mostró a la Luna hace mil años desde un huerto en el Jorasán iraní: ‘Cuantas y cuantas veces volverás a buscarme en el mismo jardín y todo será inútil’. In een toespraak achteraf was hij specifieker: Oekraïne vraagt 70 miljard euro extra van de Europese bondgenoten, "voor defensie, voor wapens en voor onze veerkracht". Zelensky's oproep komt op een moment dat Oekraïne zwaar onder druk staat. Zijn land staat aan de vooravond van een zware winter en de vrees is dat Rusland zal proberen om de Oekraïense energiesector nog harder te raken. Onder meer de hoofdstad Kyiv wordt dagelijks aangevallen met ballistische raketten en de voorraad Patriot-raketten om die projectielen tegen te houden is zo goed als op . Tijdens een persconferentie op de top in Brussel kreeg Zelensky een vraag over president Trump, die hem de afgelopen dagen meermaals heeft bekritiseerd: Bondgenoten die Oekraïne hierin willen steunen, kunnen dat maar in beperkte mate. El impacto dejó cinco muertos y, al menos, 16 heridos.Los hutíes, una guerrilla chií aliada de Irán, llevan varias semanas de ofensiva contra las tropas del Ejército regular de Yemen y también contra su vecino, Arabia Saudí. items.summary: As election day nears, two new polls show the Iran war has emerged as one of the most important issues shaping voters’ midterm decisions. National polls from Fox News and The Associated Press-NORC place the war behind only economy-related issues, government corruption, and health care among voters’ top four concerns. Significantly, the Iran war has surpassed immigration and crime, two issues on which President Donald Trump performed particularly well in 2024, among voters’ top concerns. In the 2024 campaign, pre - and post -election polling showed those issues as ranking higher as a priority for voters than foreign policy. The Fox News survey showed 75% of respondents were either “extremely” (42%) or “very” (33%) concerned about the war in Iran. items.summary: Gulf states have downplayed damage caused by Iranian strikes: Report Arabian Gulf monarchies have “suppressed” information about the extent of damage done to their physical infrastructure by attacks from Iran and its allies, Reuters reported on Thursday. Gulf states such as Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait faced thousands of missile and drone strikes launched by Iran in retaliation for the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on 28 February. More recently, Saudi Arabia has come under attack from the Houthis in Yemen. The Houthis and Iran targeted civilian infrastructure like pipelines, energy facilities and, in one case, a nuclear energy plant. Reuters' assessment is likely to cast new doubt on how Gulf states describe strikes on their territories. For example, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said that a Houthi drone strike caused a "limited fire" at the headquarters of the kingdom's national oil company, Aramco, in Dhahran. But Reuters reported on Wednesday that the headquarters suffered “extensive damage”. Readmore: Gulf states have downplayed damage caused by Iranian strike

Iran’s deputy legal affairs minister called for Israel to be expelled from CICA following Herzog's speech in Baku. Kazem Gharibabadi was quoted as saying by Iran's IRIB news that “sustainable security” in Asia was not achieved through “threats and pressure, but through mutual respect, trust-building and equal cooperation among independent states”. “If the international community does not stop America and Israel today, their aggression will spread to all independent countries. clusters.headline: Gulf economies will not return to pre-war growth soon, IMF warns

items.title: Gulf economies will not return to pre-war growth soon, IMF warns
items.summary: Gulf economies will not return to pre-war growth soon, IMF warns The International Monetary Fund (IMF) expects Middle Eastern economies to bounce back, but not in the medium term, the organisation's regional chief said on Thursday. "We will not go back to the pre-war trajectory in the medium term because this shock will have a scarring impact on various sectors and also will disrupt a certain number of infrastructure, and will require additional spending in order to increase resilience," IMF regional director Jihad Azour told reporters. The warning comes as officials and experts huddled in Bangkok this week to discuss headwinds facing the global economy, including stubbornly high energy costs. Chinese buyers have secured at least 80 million barrels of Saudi crude since mid-September, Kpler said on X. China’s onshore crude inventories fell by about 1.6 million barrels per day in September, the fastest pace on record. Refinery throughput is projected to reach 14.2 million barrels per day by December, adding to pressure on refiners to rebuild stocks. At the same time, Chinese refiners need to replace roughly 1 million barrels per day of Iranian supply, with the US blockade still in place, according to Kpler. Stronger Chinese demand could limit further weakness in Dubai crude pricing, particularly as escalating regional tensions continue to threaten supply flows.

items.summary: The Iran war was a central point of tension in Senate debates Tuesday night. As the issue becomes harder to avoid, Republican candidates in Iowa and Maine have signaled a break with President Donald Trump and his war. Now, they are being pressed on something tougher than whether they want the conflict over: what they would actually do to end it. Iowa is one of the typically red states now playing host to a razor-close race in 2026. The war’s economic fallout has been a particularly potent political issue in Iowa, perhaps because the state’s gas prices have jumped 69% — tied for the nation’s largest increase , according to AAA data from late August — and because it is among the country’s most farming-dependent states. Two of the state’s Republican U.S. representatives, Mariannette Miller-Meeks and Zach Nunn, recently became the sixth and seventh members of their party’s House caucus to support Iran war powers resolutions, which would limit Trump’s ability to go to war without congressional approval. Dat zegt de Oekraïense president Zelensky. Hij wijst erop dat zijn leger geen aanvallen heeft uitgevoerd op Russische olieraffinaderijen en de energiesector, zoals Trump wilde. "Maar Rusland heeft geen gehoor gegeven aan de Amerikaanse president", aldus Zelensky. Volgens de president hebben de Russen zowel energiecentrales als cruciale infrastructuur aangevallen. "Daarmee hebben ze volstrekt duidelijk aangetoond dat ze niet van plan zijn af te zien van aanvallen op Oekraïne." At the time of writing, the missile strike on King Khalid international airport has killed at least 13 people and left 300 injured, marking a significant turn in a regional conflagration that is only getting more intense. It was the single most deadly attack on any Gulf country since the US and Israel launched their war on Iran in February. In Saudi Arabia, a country that is unaccustomed to such fatalities, the death toll is bewilderingly high and likely to prompt a bloody response. Over the past year, the Gulf has entered a new era of instability that is not temporary and cannot be reversed. His sharpest critics see this as ranging from sycophantic revenge on the general officer class to simply misguided personnel policy. Hegseth defined it in his speech as “accountability and long overdue.” That accountability he’s referring to speaks to a symptom of a much larger problem within the general officer class, a feeling that our nation’s military leaders at times get over their skis. items.title: Two Indian nationals missing after drone attack on tanker off Oman's coast
items.summary: Two Indian nationals missing after drone attack on tanker off Oman's coast A drone attack on a vessel off the coast of Oman left two Indian nations missing, a senior Indian official said on Sunday. Meanwhile, nine others were rescued, as search and rescue operations by the local coast guard begin. "On Oct 11, tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was subjected to a drone attack at Sohar Anchorage," Indian Shipping Minister Sarbananda Sonowal said in a post on X. "While nine of our Indian crew members have been successfully rescued and are safe, two Indian nationals currently remain missing." Sonowal added that India is "continuously coordinating with all relevant authorities to fully support the ongoing rescue efforts and ensure every possible action is taken to safely locate our missing personnel". Since the war on Iran began in late February, at least 16 Indian seafarers have been killed.

The poll also found that majorities or strong pluralities of 3,200 respondents in the six states favor “cutting $3.3 billion in taxpayer-funded weapons to Israel” and believe the war in Iran benefits Israel more than the United States. items.summary: During the ongoing conflict between Iran and the United States, the Arab Gulf states have borne the brunt of Iranian drone and missile strikes while incurring mounting economic costs. With limited prospects for a U.S.-Iran settlement, Gulf states, using Oman as an interlocutor , have pursued talks with Iran aimed at ending the conflict and reopening the Strait of Hormuz to commercial shipping. This reflects a significant shift in regional dynamics: Gulf states are increasingly exploring arrangements with Iran to restore navigation without direct U.S. involvement. Even without U.S. acquiescence, securing a negotiated agreement will be difficult. Distrust between the Arab Gulf states and Iran runs deep, rooted in historic grievances and long-term contestation for hegemony in the Middle East. The ongoing conflict has intensified hostility and resentment on both sides. But the conflict has also revealed the Gulf states’ vulnerability while underscoring the limits of the U.S. security umbrella. items.title: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen government camp rises to 73
items.summary: Death toll from Houthi strike on Yemen government camp rises to 73 Local Yemeni authorities on Tuesday raised the death toll from a Houthi strike a day earlier on a military camp belonging to government forces to 73, as fighting between the foes escalates. It marked the deadliest attack in weeks as fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and Yemen's internationally recognised, Saudi-supported government rages after the collapse of a years-long truce. The death toll from Monday's strike on the camp in the energy-rich Shabwa province "increased to 73 martyrs, while search and follow-up efforts are ongoing to discover the fate of 14 missing people", authorities said in a statement. Local authorities had put the death toll at 53 on Monday, adding that more than 200 others were injured, all new members of the internal security forces who were undergoing training.

IRGC says three tankers hit mines crossing Hormuz Strait
items.summary: IRGC says three tankers hit mines crossing Hormuz Strait Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) said on Tuesday that its naval mines halted three tankers attempting to travel the Strait of Hormuz via routes considered illegal by Tehran. "Two violating oil tankers were set ablaze and halted due to the explosion of mines planted by the brave sailors of the IRGC Navy at an illegal crossing point in the southern part of the Strait of Hormuz," the IRGC said in a statement on its official Sepah News website. The Guard later said in a statement carried by state TV that a third oil tanker "exploded and caught fire after striking a naval mine south of the Strait of Hormuz". The statement added that the tanker, "carrying over 2 million barrels of crude oil, had deactivated all of its radar and navigation systems".

items.title: Iran security chief rejects moving enriched uranium out of country
items.summary: Iran security chief rejects moving enriched uranium out of country Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei on Tuesday told the visiting Pakistani army chief Asim Munir that Tehran would not allow nuclear material to leave the country, according to state TV. "Not even a tiny bit of enriched nuclear material will leave Iran; such materials constitute a major asset and national wealth for the Iranian people, intended for use within the country," said Rezaei, Iran's secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. "There will be no negotiations until America takes steps to build trust - a process that must begin with the fulfilment of Iran's conditions," he added. Iran's chief negotiator and parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf made similar remarks to Munir, who is in Tehran as part of a renewed push to mediate a peace deal between the Islamic Republic and the United States.

items.title: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz
items.summary: UN demands aid access to besieged Yemen city Taiz The United Nations insisted on Tuesday that aid must immediately be allowed to enter Yemen's Taiz, besieged by Iran-aligned Houthi fighters who are preventing supplies from reaching the country's third-largest city. Houthi fighters have encircled Taiz since early October, blocking the road that links it to Aden, interim capital of the Saudi-backed, internationally recognised government. "Humanitarian aid must be immediately allowed to enter the city and its passage must be facilitated," UN human rights chief Volker Turk said in a statement. He said relief must reach the city to avert a rights catastrophe. "The Houthis' closure of the only supply route linking Taiz to Aden is placing civilians at grave risk, blocking humanitarian aid and cutting off essential supplies," said Turk.

The vessel violated Iran-imposed “regulations” by switching off its navigation system while transiting the waterway, the IRGC said. “An illicit oil tanker exploded and caught fire in its engine room after hitting a naval mine in the southern Strait of Hormuz,” the Fars news agency quoted the IRGC as saying. “If ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf switch off their navigation and identification systems, they will be dealt with severely and decisively.”

Rubio said the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis. The United Arab Emirates has agreed to re-enter the Yemen conflict by resuming payments to some government forces fighting Iran-aligned Houthis in the south, according to sources in Yemen. In return, Saudi Arabia has agreed to provide air cover for the anti-Houthi force. The new cooperation agreement is the first tangible sign that the deep rift between the UAE and Saudi Arabia over Yemen’s future is starting to be healed – if only because the advance by Houthi forces across Yemen has alarmed all the rival Gulf state rulers. items.title: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief
items.summary: Hormuz controlled by US and allies, not Iran: Centcom chief The Strait of Hormuz "is controlled by the United States and our regional partners, not Iran ", the head of US Central Command (Centcom) has said. In a video statement, Centcom commander Brad Cooper said the US blockade of Iranian ports had imposed "a devastating cost" on the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). He said it had completely halted Iran's maritime exports and imports, "with the exception of humanitarian assistance we have allowed in". Cooper said the US had "prevented Iran from exporting at least 25 billion dollars worth of crude oil" and had "significantly degraded Iran's ability to project power far beyond its borders". He added that US forces had helped Gulf allies ship more than 100 million barrels of crude through the strait in the past week, with around 400 merchant vessels passing through. In total, the US had helped regional partners move 1.3 billion barrels through Hormuz in recent months, he said.

items.summary: Dice Andrés Trapiello que la poesía no ha muerto, esto es que vive, pero no así el mundo que la necesitaba. Lo dice, a su manera, para celebrar un aniversario de la editorial La Veleta, que el escritor fundó hace ahora cien libros de poemas, después de otras aventuras editoriales, como Trieste. Y lo celebra con la publicación de las traducciones de Emily Dickinson que debemos a Carlos Pujol, lector y traductor y persona inmejorable. O muchos versos: la flor que el arado destroza en el poema de Catulo, las cuatro personas para las que escribía Pound (¡oh mundo, lo siento por ti!), la tumba en el aire que excavan los judíos de la ‘Fuga de la muerte’ de Celan, o el combatiente ejecutado ante los ojos de René Char, caído como una hoja que una ráfaga de viento arrastraría... Significantly, the Iran war has surpassed immigration and crime, two issues on which President Donald Trump performed particularly well in 2024, among voters’ top concerns. The Saudi capital's international airport has been targeted by strikes 20 times since the beginning of the month, with an attack last weekend killing 13 people and wounding more than 300. In a joint statement shared by the Security Council's president, Greece's Evangelos Sekeris, the 15-member UN body also condemned "continued Houthi attacks and threats against commercial shipping in the Red Sea and Bab al-Mandab (Strait)". The statement also "affirmed the inherent right of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia of self-defence in accordance with international law."

Gulf states such as Qatar, the UAE, Bahrain, and Kuwait faced thousands of missile and drone strikes launched by Iran in retaliation for the US-Israeli attack on the Islamic Republic on 28 February. More recently, Saudi Arabia has come under attack from the Houthis in Yemen. The Houthis and Iran targeted civilian infrastructure like pipelines, energy facilities and, in one case, a nuclear energy plant. Reuters' assessment is likely to cast new doubt on how Gulf states describe strikes on their territories. For example, Saudi Arabia’s energy ministry said that a Houthi drone strike caused a "limited fire" at the headquarters of the kingdom's national oil company, Aramco, in Dhahran. items.summary: Chinese refiners rush to buy Middle East crude as stocks fall, Kpler says Chinese refiners are stepping up purchases of Middle Eastern crude as record inventory drawdowns and a recovery in refinery activity boost demand for prompt cargoes, according to analytics firm Kpler. Chinese buyers have secured at least 80 million barrels of Saudi crude since mid-September, Kpler said on X. China’s onshore crude inventories fell by about 1.6 million barrels per day in September, the fastest pace on record. Refinery throughput is projected to reach 14.2 million barrels per day by December, adding to pressure on refiners to rebuild stocks. At the same time, Chinese refiners need to replace roughly 1 million barrels per day of Iranian supply, with the US blockade still in place, according to Kpler. Zardari called for differences to be resolved through dialogue and diplomacy, emphasising the importance of safe maritime navigation through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea, according to a statement from his office. Kolokoltsev is on a four-day official visit to Pakistan, the first by a Russian interior minister to the South Asian country.

items.title: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says
items.summary: Attacks on Hormuz shipping at wartime high, report says Iranian missile and drone attacks on ships in and around the Strait of Hormuz were at their most intense in the two weeks to 11 October, the highest level since the US-Israeli strikes began seven months ago, the Financial Times reported. The next most intense period of attacks was during the first two weeks of March, when 13 ships were hit, the newspaper said, citing data from naval agency UK Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO), which monitors marine security in the region. Shipowners are reconsider carrying cargoes in the region, the report said. Six vessels were attacked on Sunday alone, making it the deadliest day of attacks on shipping near the strait since the start of the conflict, FT calculated. It added that oil shipments through Hormuz fell to just 2.9 million barrels on 11 October, the lowest daily volume this month, according to Kpler.

items.title: Why Saudi Arabia has returned to war in Yemen
items.summary: This article was republished with permission from the Arab Center Washington DC. When Ansar Allah—commonly referred to as the Houthis— seized Yemen’s Red Sea coastline and strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandab Strait on September 10, 2026, they appeared to gain the upper hand in Yemen’s long-running conflict. However, in early October Saudi-backed government forces began to retake some of the captured territory and Saudi Arabia launched a punishing assault on Houthi positions from the air. France , Pakistan , and the United States have all sent personnel to help the kingdom counter the Houthi offensive.
